skill.name: controlnet-pose
skill.description: Choose a RunComfy model to generate images from pose, depth, or edge references, or transfer motion from a video to a target character. The skill uses the RunComfy CLI and points to ComfyUI workflows when a project needs multiple controls.
skill.summary: Generate images from pose references or transfer video motion to a target character with RunComfy.
skill.author: prime-skills

security_audit.summary: All 62 static alerts are false positives for the behavior they flag, including Markdown backticks, reference URLs, and documented CLI authentication. The skill does recommend unpinned CLI installation, show fragile shell quoting, and omit a confirmation step for cloud disclosure. No evidence of prompt injection or credential theft was found in the reviewed skill.

remediation.issue: Inline shell examples can mishandle untrusted input.
remediation.suggestion: Replace inline interpolation with JSON serialization and pass the payload as a single argument through a non-shell process interface. Remove the claim that JSON eliminates shell injection.

remediation.issue: CLI setup installs or runs an unpinned npm package.
remediation.suggestion: Pin a reviewed CLI version, verify its publisher and package integrity, and require approval before installation or execution. Prefer a preinstalled, approved CLI.

remediation.issue: Cloud submission lacks a clear confirmation step.
remediation.suggestion: Disclose that RunComfy receives the prompt and media URLs. Obtain explicit approval before submitting private material, and warn that signed URLs may grant access.

semantic_findings.title: Unsafe Shell Argument Construction
semantic_findings.description: The Bash examples put JSON inside shell quotes and invite substitution of user prompts and URLs. JSON serialization alone does not protect the surrounding shell argument. Unsafe substitution could result in local command execution.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The examples show the shell quoting boundary, while the security note dismisses it based on CLI behavior. The impact depends on how the agent constructs arguments.

semantic_findings.title: Unpinned CLI Installation and Execution
semantic_findings.description: Setup suggests installing the latest npm release globally or executing it with automatic confirmation. A compromised release could run with the installing user's permissions.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Both documented commands omit a version, and the alternative uses automatic confirmation. The concern is the installation policy, not evidence of a compromised package.

semantic_findings.title: Cloud Disclosure Without Explicit Confirmation
semantic_findings.description: The CLI submits prompts and reference URLs to RunComfy. The skill limits inputs to user-provided URLs but does not require approval to share private media or signed links with the service.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The examples identify the data sent, and the security section requires user-provided URLs without a separate disclosure check. No covert destination is shown.

content.user_title: Guide Image and Video Generation with Pose References
content.value_statement: Text prompts alone can make it hard to reproduce a specific pose or motion. This skill chooses a RunComfy model that uses a control image or reference video to guide generation.
actual_capabilities: Choose Kling Motion Control Pro or Standard to transfer motion from a reference video onto a target character image.
Recommend community Wan 2-2 Animate for stylized character animation with audio and pose conditioning.
Use Z-Image Turbo ControlNet LoRA with a prompt and a compatible pose, depth, or Canny edge control image.
Submit a job through the RunComfy CLI, poll its status, and download the result to a local output directory.
Point to RunComfy ComfyUI workflows when a request needs multiple controls, such as pose and depth.
limitations: Generation uses the RunComfy cloud and requires an installed CLI, network access, and authentication.
The CLI does not extract OpenPose or DWPose skeletons from photos. Prepare the control image separately and provide a URL.
The documented CLI routes use a single control. Stacking pose, depth, and other controls requires a separate ComfyUI workflow.
Motion transfer may not preserve fine facial details in photoreal characters.

use_cases.title: Illustrate a Specific Stance
use_cases.description: Use a prepared OpenPose skeleton to guide a character illustration while the prompt describes the outfit and setting.

use_cases.title: Preview Character Motion
use_cases.description: Transfer a rehearsal clip onto an approved character image with Kling Standard, then consider Pro for the final version.

use_cases.title: Evaluate a Mascot Animation Route
use_cases.description: Check whether the community Wan Animate model fits a stylized mascot project that needs audio and pose guidance.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Model for a Still Image
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: Identify the right model before preparing assets.
prompt_templates.prompt: I want to generate a still illustration from an OpenPose skeleton. Recommend a RunComfy model and list the inputs I need. Do not submit a job.

prompt_templates.title: Generate a Pose-Guided Still
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: Generate an illustration with a prepared control image.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this approved OpenPose image URL to guide a stylized illustration of a gardener. Confirm the model and data sent to RunComfy before submitting. Put the result in ./out.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a Motion Transfer
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: Preview a continuous action on a different character.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use my rehearsal video for motion and my character image for appearance. Recommend whether Kling Standard is suitable for the draft. Ask before submitting either URL to RunComfy.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Multi-Control Workflow
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: Combine pose and depth in a ComfyUI project.
prompt_templates.prompt: I need both an OpenPose skeleton and a depth map to guide one image. Recommend a RunComfy ComfyUI workflow and list the assets to prepare. Do not submit a CLI job.

output_examples.input: I have an OpenPose skeleton and want a still illustration in the same stance.
output_examples.output: Use Z-Image Turbo ControlNet LoRA. Provide a hosted OpenPose control image and a text prompt describing the subject and scene.

output_examples.input: I want a draft of my illustrated character performing the movement in a rehearsal clip.
output_examples.output: Use Kling Motion Control Standard for the draft. The rehearsal clip supplies the movement, and the character image supplies the appearance.

output_examples.input: I need a still image to follow both a pose skeleton and a depth map.
output_examples.output: Use a multi-condition ComfyUI workflow in RunComfy instead of a single-control CLI route. Prepare the pose skeleton and depth map as separate assets.

best_practices: Use a well-framed motion reference with one subject, one continuous action, and no scene cuts.
Check the current model schema to confirm that the LoRA supports your control image type.
Confirm what will be sent to RunComfy and use only media you have permission to share.
anti_patterns: Passing a raw photo to a route that expects a precomputed pose skeleton.
Sending both a pose map and a depth map to a documented single-control CLI route.
Pasting untrusted prompts or media URLs into a shell command.

faq.question: What do I need to run a generation job?
faq.answer: You need the RunComfy CLI, network access, a signed-in RunComfy account, and the inputs required by the selected model.

faq.question: Which Kling tier should I use for motion transfer?
faq.answer: Use Standard for early drafts and iteration. The skill recommends Pro for final video delivery.

faq.question: Can the skill extract an OpenPose skeleton from my photo?
faq.answer: No. Create the skeleton with a separate OpenPose or DWPose preprocessor, then provide the control image URL.

faq.question: Can I guide one image with both pose and depth?
faq.answer: Yes, through a suitable ComfyUI workflow. The documented CLI image route is for a single control.

faq.question: What information does RunComfy receive?
faq.answer: RunComfy receives the job inputs, including prompts and media URLs when the selected model uses them. Confirm before submitting private assets or signed links.

faq.question: Where does the generated file go?
faq.answer: The CLI downloads results to the specified local output directory. The documented examples use ./out.
